senses.gloss:
Lakṣa in the Rigveda denotes the ‘prize’ at dicing.
Foot notes ii. 12, 4. Cf. Lüders, Das Würfelspiel im alten Indien, 4, n. 1; Zimmer. Altindisches Leben, 287.

Lākṣā occurs once in the Atharvaveda as the name of a plant.
Foot notes v. 5, 7. Cf. Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 229; Bloomfield, Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 387, 421.

Lakṣaṇa or lakṣman denotes the ‘mark’ made on cattle by branding to distinguish ownership. According to the Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, it was to be made under the nakṣatra revatī, clearly because of the property indicated in the name (‘wealthy’) of that nakṣatra. See aṣṭakarṇī.
Foot notes Gobhila gṛhya sūtra, iii. 6, 5. Cf. śāṅkhāyana gṛhya sūtra, iii. 10; Weber, Indische Studien, 5, 35; 13, 466.
Av. vi. 141, 2; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iv. 2, 9.
Loc. cit.

Lakṣmaṇya in one verse of the Rigveda seems to be a patronymic of dhvanya, ‘son of Lakṣmaṇa.’
Foot notes v. 33, 10. Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 155.
